We also tested whether the Homo-BacPROTACs would be comparably active in a reconstituted degradation assay in which the three Msm proteins were replaced by their corresponding Mth homologues.

To this end, various Homo BacPROTACs, their distomers, and matching monomeric compounds were tested in the Mth cell-free degradation assay and we observed Homo-BacPROTAC-mediated degradation of the CipCI-NTD (Supplementary Table 8), with comparable DCso values and slightly reduced Dax Values as seen for Msm CIpCIPIP2. As expected, the control compounds did not cause degradation.

We also analyzed whether full-length CIpCI would be degraded in this assay, by analyzing the stability of the full-length form monitored by a CIpIN-terminal antibody in the WES assays, or directly by SYPRO™ Ruby stained SDS-PAGE gels in the presence or absence of CIpCI-NTD as additional substrate. The Homo-BacPROTACs tested induced no or only minor degradation of the full-length CIpC1 under these in vitro conditions (Fig. 4e). Whether this is due to hexamer formation stabilizing CIpCI protomers or missing cofactor(s) of the protease complex, is currently unclear. Likewise, the exact sequential and structural features of native substrates targeted by ClpC1 are not known, except that partially disordered peptide segments can promote degradation".

Homo-BacPROTACs induce degradation of endogenous ClpC1 in Msm

Irrespective of the behavior of Homo-BacPROTACs in cell-free assay systems, we wanted to assess their potential to degrade endogenous CIpCI in Msm. Using a capillary Western-based cellular degradation assay, we could show that Homo-BacPROTAC 8 (UdSBI-0545) induced degradation with an average DCso of 0.57 +0.40uM and an average Dnax of 48 + 13% after 24 h of incubation in a concentration-dependent manner (Fig. Sa), while the enantiomeric control Sa (UdSBI-0966) did not lead to intracellular degradation of ClpC1 (Fig. 5b). Homo- BacPROTAC 12 (UdSBI-4377) also induced full-length CIpC1 degradation (average DCso 0.17 + 0.10 pM; average Dmax 43 + 8%), while its enantiomer 12a (UdSBI-0117) was inactive (Fig. 5b). In addition, the matching monomers 5, 10 and CymC did not induce degradation of ClpC1 (Fig. 5c).
